findings.text: During a pagetable walk for smaps accounting, the middle-level handler first attempts a transparent huge fast path under its dedicated lock and delegates to the huge-aware helper, otherwise maps the leaf table with its lock, requests a walk retry if the mapping is unavailable, iterates page by page over the range invoking the per-entry accounting helper, then releases the mapping and yields the CPU before reporting success.

Area flag output starts with a fixed label, then for each bit position that carries a non-empty mnemonic and is set in the area flags appends that mnemonic plus a separator, finally emitting a newline; unknown positions show a placeholder, several privileged or arch-specific positions deliberately use empty mnemonics to suppress output, and table dimensions and entries vary with word size and kernel configuration.

For hugetlb entries the walker locks the huge entry, samples it once, resolves a present entry to its folio and marks presence, otherwise attempts a soft-leaf conversion and keeps a folio only when a frame number is encoded, then charges the full huge page size to a shared counter when non-present or possibly shared or marked shared, else to a private counter, before unlocking.
An alternative build configuration provides no hugetlb callback for smaps walks, so the corresponding hook is absent.

Four pagetable-walk operation tables share the same middle-level and hugetlb callbacks; two add a hole callback for shmem accounting, and the pairs differ only in the requested walk locking mode, one using a global read mode and the other a per-area verified read mode.

One build selects the walk table dynamically based on whether the caller already holds the address-space read lock, preferring the global-lock table when held and the per-area verified table otherwise, for both normal and shmem variants; the alternate build unconditionally returns the global-lock tables.

Statistics gathering for one area ignores out-of-range starts and a special gate area, temporarily drops an outer read guard while keeping the area pinned, uses an efficient swap-usage shortcut for eligible shmem mappings based on start offset and shared or writability attributes and otherwise switches to the hole-aware walk, then walks either the whole area or a suffix starting at the given offset before reacquiring the guard.

The common smaps counter renderer emits resident, proportional set sizes, shared and private clean and dirty, referenced, anonymous, deduplicated, lazy-free, transparent huge, shmem and file middle-level mapped, shared and private hugetlb, swap, swap proportional, and locked amounts in kilobytes in a fixed order, with three extra proportional breakdowns present only in rollup mode.

Per-area smaps output first collects statistics from the start of the area, prints the mapping header, reports byte size plus kernel and MMU page sizes, delegates to the common counter renderer in non-rollup mode, then adds a transparent-huge eligibility flag and, when protection keys are active, a key identifier, followed by the flags line.

Rollup mode resolves the target task and its address space with reference counting, locks it, snapshots the memory policy, iterates all areas accumulating statistics from each start, and on lock contention invalidates the iterator, releases and reacquires the lock, then resumes by skipping freed areas, continuing after unchanged areas, or re-entering a split area from the previous end; with no areas it emits an empty range, otherwise a single header labelled rollup plus aggregated counters, then releases policy, lock and references.

Smaps sequence handling iterates areas with start, next and stop helpers and a per-area show routine, while the regular and rollup file operations wire open, sequential read, seek and release to area-specific versus rollup-specific open and release helpers.

Rollup open allocates a private context with accounting, attaches it to a single-show sequence, records the inode, opens the target address space in read mode and on failure releases the sequence and frees the context returning an appropriate error; release drops the address-space reference when present, frees the context and completes single-release.
Clear-references commands are numbered consecutively from one for all, anonymous-only, file-mapped-only, soft-dirty, and high-water reset, with a following sentinel marking the end of valid values.
Clear-references walk context carries only the requested command selector.

A table entry is considered pinned only when it is writable in a copy-on-write area of an address space flagged as containing pinned pages and its resolved normal folio reports possible direct-access pinning; any earlier negative test yields unpinned.

Soft-dirty clearing for a single entry is a no-op when the architecture lacks support or the entry is empty; present entries that are not pinned are transitioned through a modify-protect window to become write-protected and clean, while non-present entries have their swapped soft-dirty state cleared and are rewritten.

For huge middle-level entries one build preserves dirty and young state across an invalidate, then write-protects and clears soft-dirty before reinstalling, and clears swapped soft-dirty for migration entries, all skipped when unsupported; the alternate build defines the helper as doing nothing.

The clear-references middle-level handler takes a huge fast path that either clears huge soft-dirty state or, when present, clears young state in both the table entry and folio plus the referenced mark; the regular path maps the leaf table with retry on failure, then per page either clears soft-dirty or, for present entries with a normal folio, clears young and referenced state, finally releasing the mapping and yielding.

Clear-references walks skip areas that are raw frame maps, restrict anonymous-only commands to areas without a backing file and mapped-only commands to areas with one, and run under an exclusive walk lock with the middle-level and test callbacks installed.

Writing to the clear-references control accepts a short decimal string, validates it against the defined command range, resolves task and address space, takes the write lock interruptibly, resets the peak resident watermark for the reset command, otherwise for soft-dirty clears the per-area soft-dirty flag and updates protection then notifies and starts invalidation over the whole range, walks the entire space with shared context, completes notification plus flush and pending-count handling for soft-dirty, unlocks and releases references returning the byte count.
The clear-references file interface exposes only write plus a no-op seek.

Pagemap entries wrap a single 64-bit value, and read state tracks a position and capacity counted in entries rather than bytes plus a buffer pointer and a flag controlling whether frame numbers are disclosed.
Pagemap walks operate in middle-level sized chunks with matching alignment mask, and each output record occupies the size of one pagemap entry.

Pagemap encoding reserves low 55 bits for frame number with matching mask; flag bit 55 marks soft dirty, 56 exclusive, 57 userfault write protect, 58 guard region, 61 file, 62 swap, 63 present; value 1 signals end of buffer.

Entry construction masks the supplied frame to the allowed width then combines flags, and appending stores at the current position, advances it, and reports buffer exhaustion once capacity is reached.
Exclusivity testing uses precise per-page mapping count equality to one when that configuration is enabled, otherwise it negates a possibly-shared heuristic.

Hole handling walks the requested interval, emitting zero entries for gaps before the next area or end of space, and for covered portions emits either zero or soft-dirty-marked entries depending on the area soft-dirty flag, stopping early when the output buffer fills.

Translation of a single table entry starts from zero frame and flags, leaves both zero for empty entries, and for present entries optionally discloses the frame number, always marks present, conditionally marks soft dirty and userfault protection, and resolves the normal page; swapped-entry handling is truncated in the routed fragment.

Smaps table walks serialize the huge fast path with its dedicated middle-level lock released via the generic unlock, serialize regular leaf iteration with a mapped leaf lock released together with unmapping, and serialize hugetlb sampling with its huge lock; the fast-path lock is not held across the regular path.

Smaps walks request either global read or verified per-area read mode selected by caller lock state, clear-references walks request exclusive mode, statistics gathering drops and reacquires an outer read guard around the walk, and rollup plus clear-references operations hold address-space read or write locks across iteration with rollup permitting temporary release on contention.

Failure to map a leaf table does not fail the walk but asks for a retry, and long leaf loops yield the processor; callers must handle repeated invocation and must not assume table stability across the yield.

Soft-dirty clearing skips pinned writable shared entries and preserves dirty and young state across huge invalidation with explicit flush and notifier bracketing; omitting the bracketing or clearing pinned entries can lose dirtiness or corrupt pinned direct-access state.

Rollup iteration that drops its lock must invalidate its iterator and recompute resume position from the last observed end because areas may have been freed, merged or split; reusing stale area pointers after reacquisition risks use-after-free or double counting.

This dossier publishes file operation tables for per-process smaps, smaps rollup and clear-references controls, exposing the corresponding open, read, seek, write and release entry points to the proc layer.
